title: C362 — Front seat track motor LH connector guide
introduction:
This reference maps the left-hand front seat track motor connection. Its function labels include forward and rearward seat movement, control-module and switch connections, and sensor connections. I read those labels separately: a seat that moves and a circuit that reports movement have different jobs, even when they share a connector. The table is the seating chart, not a command to make every occupant do the same thing.

Start with the connector identity table, then use the drawing’s cavity labels to locate the assignment rows. Read each row across for circuit identity, color, gauge, function and terminal reference. Repeated cavity entries have different circuit descriptions, but blank Qualifier cells do not tell you which equipment arrangement applies.

This page teaches reference reading rather than seat access, connector probing, wire selection or replacement. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the Size and Used code definitions remain unspecified. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the cavity count shown by the drawing and pigtail table. That count discrepancy and the meaning and applicability of the recline-sensor label remain unresolved.

edits.why: I recognize this drawing by the housing features across its top and the projection at its lower right. The cavity labels form upper and lower pairs, which can be matched directly to the Cavity column. These are positions on the supplied illustration, not an established view from the wire side or mating side. No release movement is identified.

edits.text: Read the movement and sensor assignments
edits.why: Read the forward and rearward entries with their control-module or switch descriptions attached; the shared cavity labels do not establish that those circuits are present together. The sensor rows have their own functions and terminal references. One sensor description ends with a trailing dash and refers to recline, so I retain that wording without expanding it into a polarity, signal type or seat-track operating explanation.

The service listing associates the kit with its Service Part and Engineering Shell references. I compare those fields with the connector identity information while keeping individual Terminal Part Number entries separate. The pigtail Gauge field contains multiple entries without a cavity allocation; it cannot establish which replacement wire belongs at a particular position.

originalAuthorHold: The summary Pin Count differs from the cavity count in the drawing and pigtail listing. Confirm the intended meaning of that summary field rather than equating assignment-row count with physical cavities.

The sensor function referring to recline ends with a trailing dash within a seat-track motor reference. Confirm whether the label is complete and applicable before using it to explain that circuit’s specific role.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 34 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. PinCount, repeated circuit applicability and sensor-label meaning ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
